title: Logons & accounts
summary: Failed sign-ins, lockouts and account or group changes.

events.title: An account failed to sign in
events.meaning: Someone or something tried to sign in and failed. The message shows the account, the reason and where it came from.
events.causes: A wrong password, an old saved password, or an unwanted sign-in attempt.
events.next: Check the account and source address. Many failures in a row can mean password guessing.

events.title: A user account was locked out
events.meaning: An account was locked after too many wrong passwords.
events.causes: A wrong or outdated saved password on a device or service, or guessing attempts.
events.next: Find the device named in the message that keeps sending the old password, and fix it.

events.title: Kerberos sign-in check failed
events.meaning: A domain controller refused a Kerberos sign-in request. The message holds a failure code.
events.causes: A wrong password, an expired account, or a clock that is out of sync.
events.next: Check the failure code in the message, the account status and the time sync.

events.title: The computer checked an account's password
events.meaning: A computer checked the credentials of an account using NTLM. The result tells if it passed.
events.next: Look for failures in the result code. Many failures can point to a wrong or guessed password.

events.title: A sign-in was given special privileges
events.meaning: An account with powerful rights, such as an administrator, signed in.
events.causes: Normal sign-ins by administrators or system accounts.
events.next: Only look closer if an account you do not expect has these rights.

events.title: A user account was created
events.meaning: A new account was added to the PC or domain. The message names who created it.
events.causes: An administrator or a program added an account.
events.next: Check that you expected this account and who created it.

events.title: An account password was reset
events.meaning: Someone tried to reset another account's password.
events.causes: An administrator reset a forgotten password.
events.next: Check that you expected the reset and who did it.

events.title: A member was added to a global security group
events.meaning: An account was added to a security group at the domain level.
events.next: Check that the change was expected, mainly for powerful groups.

events.title: A member was added to a local security group
events.meaning: An account was added to a group on this PC, such as Administrators.
events.causes: An administrator or an installer changed group membership.
events.next: Check that the change was expected, mainly for the Administrators group.

events.title: The Security audit log was cleared
events.meaning: The Security log was erased. The message shows who cleared it.
events.causes: An administrator cleaned the log, or someone is covering their tracks.
events.next: Check that the clearing was expected and by whom. Treat an unexpected one as a security warning.
